load_deck:
Load a Commander deck list once and get a deck id to start games with.

Automatically: Looks up every card's card data by exact name, applies your card definitions, runs the deck checks (size, singleton, color identity, legality, commander eligibility) and keeps the loaded deck. The response gives the deck id and what the service read from the cards: mana sources, step triggers, haste, vigilance and cards that enter tapped, with any assumption it made. The same list always gives the same deck id, and loading it again changes nothing.

Parameters:
- cards (required): The deck list as text, one `<count> <name>` per line; lines starting with # or // are ignored and printing details such as `(C21) 263` are dropped. Example: "1 Sol Ring\n1 Cultivate\n36 Forest"
- commander (required): The commander's name, or a list of two names for a pair of commanders. Example: "Atraxa, Praetors' Voice"
- definitions: Card definitions, each replacing the fetched card data of one card in this deck field by field: name (required), face, mana_cost, type_line, oracle_text, power, toughness, color_identity, keywords, produces (what it taps for), enters_tapped. A card Scryfall does not know needs a type_line. Example: [{"name": "Mana Vault", "produces": "{C}{C}{C}"}]
- refresh: True to fetch card data again for every card instead of using the cache. Example: true
- override: Your reason for applying the call although rule checks failed; it is recorded. Example: "testing a 99-card build on purpose"

Override: Failed deck checks can be overridden with `override`. An unparseable line, a card name that cannot be resolved, or a missing commander is an error, which cannot.
new_game:
Start a goldfish game on a loaded deck: shuffles and deals seven.

Automatically: Puts the commander in the command zone, shuffles the rest into the library using the seed, and deals seven cards. The response gives the game id, the seed and the opening hand; the game then waits for `mulligan`.

Parameters:
- deck_id (required): The deck id `load_deck` returned. Example: "df862a58edc"
- seed: The number that fixes every shuffle: the same deck and seed give the same game. The service chooses one and shows it when omitted. Example: 1234
- turn_limit: The turn whose start raises a turn-limit notice; it never stops the game. Example: 10
- draw_first_turn: False to skip the draw on turn 1; true by default. Example: false
- starting_life: Starting life of every seat; 40 by default. Example: 40

Override: Nothing; an unknown deck id is an error.
mulligan:
Keep the opening hand or take a mulligan.

Automatically: With keep false, shuffles the hand into the library and deals seven new cards. With keep true, puts the `bottom` cards on the bottom of the library in the order given (one card for each mulligan after the first, which is free), then starts the game and takes it through untap, upkeep and draw to turn 1's first main step, drawing a card unless the game was started without a first-turn draw.

Parameters:
- game_id (required): The game id `new_game` returned. Example: "gq7k2m9x4pz"
- keep: True to keep the hand, false to take a mulligan. Example: true
- bottom: When keeping after two or more mulligans, the cards from your hand to put on the bottom of the library, in order. Example: ["Island"]
- override: Your reason for applying the call although rule checks failed; it is recorded. Example: "the deck plays a free extra mulligan"
- after: The change number at the end of the last status line you saw (`#41`). A call sent twice is then applied once, and a stale picture of the game is refused. Example: 41

Override: Keeping with the wrong number of `bottom` cards is a rule check that `override` passes. A `bottom` card not in your hand, or `bottom` with keep false, is an error.
get_state:
List the hand, battlefield and other zones when the status line is not enough, or give cards' rules text.

Automatically: Changes nothing. The summary lists the hand, the battlefield (each permanent with its instance id, tapped state, counters, the mana it makes, haste or vigilance and its step triggers), the graveyard, the command zone and notices; full adds exile, the number of cards in the library, each commander's casts and damage, and this turn's payments. The library's order is never shown. With `card`, the response gives the rules text of the cards named in place of the listing. Accepted in every game status.

Parameters:
- game_id (required): The game id `new_game` returned. Example: "gq7k2m9x4pz"
- detail: "summary" (the default) or "full". Example: "full"
- card: A card name or instance id, or a list of them: the response gives each card's rules text (each face's name, mana cost, type line, rules text, and power and toughness) in place of the listing, or a token's description. Only cards you may see are answered; ask for a card in your library by name. Not given together with detail. Example: ["Sol Ring", "c12"]

Override: Nothing; it changes nothing.
play:
Play a land or cast a spell, stating what it does.

Automatically: Finds the card (in your hand, then the command zone, unless `from` says otherwise). A land uses the turn's land drop. A spell's cost — its mana cost with X, any extra cost and commander tax — is paid by the auto payment system unless `pay` says how, and the response shows what was tapped. The card then goes to its destination: a permanent to the battlefield (tapped if it enters tapped), an instant or sorcery to the graveyard. The delta is applied last. A spell's `cast_triggers` are applied once its cost is paid, in the order listed, before the card moves; one that would look or search is recorded with `effect` after the play. The library is shuffled after a fetch, a commander bound for the graveyard or exile goes to the command zone, and a token that leaves the battlefield ceases to exist.

Parameters:
- game_id (required): The game id `new_game` returned. Example: "gq7k2m9x4pz"
- card (required): The card to play: its name, a face's name, or an instance id. Example: "Cultivate"
- from: The zone it is played from: hand, command, graveyard, exile, library (found by name, nothing else disturbed) or outside (a card not in the game, looked up by name). Example: "graveyard"
- to: A destination for the card instead of its usual one, such as exile for a flashback spell. Example: "exile"
- delta: Where things end up: an object whose keys are all optional and are applied in this order, whatever order you write them in. untap: [names]. tap: [names]. mana: a mana string added to the mana pool ("{G}{G}"). tokens: [{name, count (default 1), types ("Artifact — Treasure"), pt ("1/1" or null), produces (a mana string or a list of them, what it taps for), sacrifice_to_produce, tapped}]. counters: {name: {kind: signed change}}; a kind reaching 0 is removed. move: {destination: [names]}, cards from the hand or a public zone. commander_stays: true lets a commander go to the graveyard or exile instead of the command zone. discard: [names], hand to graveyard. fetch: {destination: [names]}, cards taken from the library by name. draw: a number of cards. life: a signed change to your life. damage: noncombat damage to the opponents, pooled (2 to each opponent is 6). shuffle: true. look: {n, from: "top" or "bottom", rest: destination}, which reveals cards for a pending choice. search: {filter?}, which reveals the library sorted by name for a pending choice. A destination is hand, battlefield, battlefield_tapped, graveyard, exile, command, library_top or library_bottom. A card is named by its name, a face's name or an instance id; a name given twice means two cards. Example: {"fetch": {"battlefield_tapped": ["Plains"], "hand": ["Forest"]}}
- choices: What you announce while casting: x (the value of X), extra_cost (a mana string for kicker and the like, added to the cost), modes, targets and notes (recorded, never judged), definition (a card definition, for a card played from outside). Example: {"x": 3}
- pay: How to pay: {with?: [a source's name, or {source, mana} to say what it makes this time], cost?: a mana string replacing the whole cost, life?: life paid as part of the cost}. Sources in `with` are used first and the auto payment system pays the rest; name a Treasure or other source that is sacrificed or costs more than tapping here, since the auto payment system never uses one. Example: {"with": [{"source": "Birds of Paradise", "mana": "{U}"}]}
- cast_triggers: Your own triggers on casting this spell ("whenever you cast an instant, copy it", "when you cast this spell, draw a card"), each {source, delta, choices?}: source names what triggered, delta is what it does in the delta shape, and choices are recorded only. They resolve before the spell, in the order listed, the first listed first. A land is not cast and takes none; record a trigger on playing a land with effect. Example: [{"source": "Archmage Emeritus", "delta": {"draw": 1}}]
- expect: Values you believe hold once the call is applied; each mismatch adds a warning line and the call is applied anyway. Keys: hand, lands, untapped_lands, life, pool, library, tax, damage_dealt, step. Example: {"untapped_lands": 2, "hand": 4}
- reason: Why you made this choice, when it was not obvious; recorded in the log. Example: "holding up Counterspell mana"
- override: Your reason for applying the call although rule checks failed; it is recorded. Example: "Goblin Electromancer reduces the cost by {1}"
- after: The change number at the end of the last status line you saw (`#41`). A call sent twice is then applied once, and a stale picture of the game is refused. Example: 41

Override: Rule checks — the cost is not payable, the land drop is used, a land or a card without flash is played outside a main step, `pay` gives its own cost, a summoning-sick creature is named in `pay` — are passed with `override`. An overridden unpayable cost is played unpaid, so tap what you used with the delta's tap. Errors — a card not in the zone named, an unknown delta key, a malformed mana string — cannot be overridden.
choose:
Finish a look or search by saying where the revealed cards go.

Automatically: For a look, every revealed card you do not select goes to the look's rest destination, in `rest_order` or else in the order revealed. For a search, unselected cards stay in the library and it is shuffled before selected cards go to its top or bottom. Cards selected to library_top end with the first one named on top.

Parameters:
- game_id (required): The game id `new_game` returned. Example: "gq7k2m9x4pz"
- choice_id (required): The choice id shown with the revealed cards. Example: "x1"
- selections: Destinations mapped to revealed cards; {} selects nothing. Example: {"hand": ["Sol Ring"], "library_bottom": ["Island"]}
- rest_order: For a look, the order in which the unselected cards go to the rest destination. Example: ["Forest", "Ponder"]
- after: The change number at the end of the last status line you saw (`#41`). A call sent twice is then applied once, and a stale picture of the game is refused. Example: 41

Override: Nothing; a wrong choice id or a card that was not revealed is an error.
attack:
Declare attackers and which are blocked.

Automatically: From the first main step or beginning of combat, moves the game on to declare attackers, listing beginning-of-combat reminders on the way. Taps each attacker that has no vigilance and keeps the declared attack. When `advance` enters the combat damage step, each unblocked attacker deals its power adjusted by its +1/+1 and -1/-1 counters (or its `damage` entry) to the opponents, and an attacking commander's damage also counts as commander damage to its target opponent. An empty `attackers` clears the declared attack.

Parameters:
- game_id (required): The game id `new_game` returned. Example: "gq7k2m9x4pz"
- attackers: The attacking creatures by name or instance id; a name given twice is two creatures. Example: ["Grizzly Bears", "Atraxa, Praetors' Voice"]
- blocked: The attackers you decide the imaginary opponents block; they deal no damage. Example: ["Grizzly Bears"]
- commander_target: Which opponent (0, 1 or 2) an attacking commander attacks, 0 by default; with two attacking commanders, one number for both or {commander: number}. Example: 1
- damage: Attackers mapped to the damage each deals instead of its power, for pumps, double strike or trample. Example: {"Tarmogoyf": 5}
- vigilance: Attackers with vigilance the service has not read; for this attack only. Example: ["Serra Angel"]
- haste: Attackers with haste the service has not read; for this attack only. Example: ["Grizzly Bears"]
- reason: Why you made this choice, when it was not obvious; recorded in the log. Example: "holding back Birds of Paradise for mana"
- override: Your reason for applying the call although rule checks failed; it is recorded. Example: "Craterhoof Behemoth gave everything haste"
- after: The change number at the end of the last status line you saw (`#41`). A call sent twice is then applied once, and a stale picture of the game is refused. Example: 41

Override: Rule checks — an attacker that is not a creature, is tapped, or entered this turn without haste; a power that is not a number with no `damage` entry; attacking before the first main step, or after combat damage (an additional combat) — are passed with `override`. An attacker not on the battlefield, or a `blocked`, `damage`, `vigilance` or `haste` entry that is not among the attackers, is an error.
advance:
Move to the next step, or forward to a named step.

Automatically: Does each step's automatic actions on the way: untaps in untap, draws in draw, deals the declared attack's damage in combat damage, discards and writes the turn snapshot in cleanup, and empties the mana pool on leaving every step. Stops early, with an OK response that says why, on entering a step where one of your permanents has a step trigger (a reminder: resolve it with `effect`, or pass it), or before cleanup with more than seven cards in hand. Send `advance` again to continue.

Parameters:
- game_id (required): The game id `new_game` returned. Example: "gq7k2m9x4pz"
- to: The step to move forward to, through its next occurrence (next turn's when the game is already in it): untap, upkeep, draw, main1, begin_combat, declare_attackers, declare_blockers, combat_damage, end_combat, main2, end, cleanup. Omitted, the game moves one step. Example: "main1"
- discard: Cards in your hand to discard on entering cleanup: exactly as many as you hold over seven. Example: ["Island", "Forest"]
- override: Your reason for applying the call although rule checks failed; it is recorded. Example: "Reliquary Tower: no maximum hand size"
- after: The change number at the end of the last status line you saw (`#41`). A call sent twice is then applied once, and a stale picture of the game is refused. Example: 41

Override: Entering cleanup with more than seven cards in hand and no `discard`, or a `discard` of the wrong number, is a rule check that `override` passes. An unknown step, a `discard` card not in your hand, or `discard` on an advance that does not enter cleanup is an error.
end_game:
End the game with a result and verdict.

Automatically: Discards any pending choice and declared attack, writes the turn snapshot if this turn has none, and ends the game; afterwards only `get_state` and `get_log` are accepted.

Parameters:
- game_id (required): The game id `new_game` returned. Example: "gq7k2m9x4pz"
- result (required): win, loss or stalled. Example: "win"
- notes: Your verdict: what the deck did well and what it did badly. Example: "Won on turn 8 with Craterhoof; the hand was short of green sources early."
- after: The change number at the end of the last status line you saw (`#41`). A call sent twice is then applied once, and a stale picture of the game is refused. Example: 41

Override: Nothing; your result is trusted.
get_log:
Return the game's records as JSON for analysis.

Automatically: Changes nothing. Returns {game, entries, snapshots, calls}: the log entries of accepted changes with your choices and reasons, the turn snapshots, and the call records when asked for. Accepted in every game status. A call that cannot be answered is an ERROR in the text format, not JSON.

Parameters:
- game_id (required): The game id `new_game` returned. Example: "gq7k2m9x4pz"
- since: Only records after this change number. Example: 20
- tools: A list of tool names: keeps only the log entries and call records of calls to those tools, leaving the snapshots as they would be without it. Example: ["play", "attack"]
- include_snapshots: False to leave the turn snapshots out; true by default. Example: false
- include_calls: True to include the call records; false by default. Example: true

Override: Nothing; it changes nothing. An empty `tools`, or one naming anything that is not a tool, is an error.
